title: Notification Fanout UX proposal v0
content:
Purpose:
This draft captures an opinionated UX for the notification fanout and alert policy composer in the Console. Goal is to make it fast for engineers to:
- map SLO alerts to multiple delivery channels,
- configure thresholds and dedup/fanout rules, and
- reason about who gets notified under which conditions (and why).

Background / problem statement:
- Current Console shows alerts & SLOs in separate places; channel configuration is buried. Teams end up creating ad-hoc slack hooks or relying on infra runbooks.
- Common requests from customers: route the SAME SLO alert to different channels depending on severity, environment, and on-call rotation; ensure low-noise for transient perf blips; provide visible fallbacks (email when Slack fails).

Design goals:
1) Single composer: define an alert policy once and attach SLOs/metrics + multiple channels.
2) Predictable fanout and dedup: clear primary channel, escalation path, and dedup windows.
3) Quick presets: templates for common stacks (pager + slack + email + webhook).
4) Traceability: show sample event timeline for a policy so users can preview who gets pinged.
5) Low cognitive load: progressive disclosure — basic config up-front, advanced rules in an expandable panel.

Proposed UX surface (high level):
- Left: Policy selector (list of policies, filter by team/model/environment). Quick actions: duplicate, mute, run test.
- Center: Composer canvas
  - Header: policy name, team, global toggle (enabled/disabled), severity tag (info/warn/critical).
  - Bindings area: SLOs & metrics pinned to this policy (drag-and-drop from right pane).
  - Thresholds block: friendly presets (p95 latency > 500ms), and an advanced expression editor.
  - Dedup & suppression: sliding window input (e.g., "suppress duplicates for 10m") and noise reduction toggle (auto-suppress transient spikes).
- Right: Channels & fanout panel
  - Channel list: checkboxes for each destination (Slack, PagerDuty, Email, Webhook, Opsgenie).
  - For each channel: per-channel overrides (severity threshold, rate limit, formatting template).
  - Escalation chain builder: compact vertical list; add step > select target > set delay > add condition (e.g., escalate if not acknowledged in 5m).
  - Fallback rule: choose a fallback channel if primary returns 5xx or times out.

Preview & reasoning panel (bottom):
- Simulate: run with a sample incident to show derived fanout events.
- Delivery timeline: visual timeline with icons for each channel (shows dedupe & escalation).
- Evidence: links to the SLO and recent samples that would trigger this policy.

Wireframe notes (sketch-level):
- Use a 3-column layout (policies / composer / channels) that collapses to 2 columns on narrow screens.
- Composer blocks are modular cards: thresholds, dedupe, bindings, annotations. Cards can be re-ordered.
- Each channel row shows status (connected, rate-limited, last test) and quick-test button.
- Mini-map: top-right corner miniature indicates which part of the policy is being edited.

Microcopy / labels suggestions:
- "Primary channel" = first fanout target; "Escalation" = subsequent targets if not acknowledged.
- Tooltips: explain "dedup window" vs "suppression window" (examples).
- Button: "Run policy test" with a warning that this will send test messages to live channels unless toggled to sandbox.

Example flows (three):
1) Production p95 breach -> Slack #prod-incidents + PagerDuty; dedupe 10m; escalate to on-call manager after 15m if unacknowledged.
2) Staging flakiness -> Email only, low severity, suppressed for 30m if recurring.
3) ML model quality SLO drop -> Webhook to monitoring pipeline + slack alert to model-owner; if webhook fails, fallback to email.

Edge cases & constraints:
- Channel rate limits: UI must surface downstream rate limit errors (e.g., Slack 429).
- Cross-team policies: if policy references SLOs owned by other teams, require read/notify-only binding unless explicit cross-team grant exists.
- Private deployments: VPC webhook targets need validator steps (cert thumbprint).

Backlog / grooming items (initial):
- PIPE-4901: Policy composer scaffold + 3-column layout (2w) [prio: P0] -> owner: Ethan
- PIPE-4922: Channel status & quick-test UX (1w) [P1] -> owner: Lina
- PIPE-4930: Dedup & suppression logic UI + backend API (2w) [P0] -> owner: Gabe
- PIPE-4955: Escalation chain editor (drag to reorder) (1.5w) [P1] -> owner: Samira
- PIPE-4980: Sandbox test mode + simulated delivery preview (3w) [P1] -> owner: Priya
- PIPE-4999: Preset templates (pager+slack+email) and template marketplace (0.5w) [P2] -> owner: Product

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Users can create a policy, bind at least one SLO, and add two channels.
- Dedup window configurable and respected in simulation.
- Escalation step triggers after configured delay in simulated run.
- Quick-test returns delivery status for each channel (success/failure).

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Should per-channel formatting use templating language (handlebars-style) or structured fields? (tradeoff: flexibility vs complexity)
- How do we represent overlapping policies that both fire for same SLO? (do we dedupe across policies?)
- Default dedup window value — 10 minutes seems reasonable but needs validation from SREs.
- For hosted customers, do we expose raw webhook response codes in the Console or sanitize?

Next steps (short):
- Run 30-min design review with SRE, Platform, and Solutions Eng (scheduled 2024-10-08).
- Create Figma screens for composer + channel panel (Ethan).
- Backend contract proposal for dedupe/suppression API (Gabe).
- Add small user-research session with 3 customers who manage >=2 on-call rotations (Priya).

Notes to self / quick todos:
- Add a small glossary section in Console for "dedup window", "suppression", "escalation".
- Add example JSON payload for webhook channel in docs.
- Link policy to Audit logs entry for every change.

References:
- sample alert templates in /shared-drives/customer-success/alert-templates (link TODO)
- internal PagerDuty integration docs (confluence link TODO)

--
End of draft. This is intentionally sketchy: focus on minimal, testable scope for MVP then iterate.
